g.text: refreshFrame, copy "ready" framebuffer to screen framebuffer
swapBuffers, does the OS window swap. Which will not do
much, as the screen should be running in singlebuffer mode.
The refresh is always done on the main thread.
Layout changes generate animations, if that is enabled.
Animations are running at the desired Framerate.
Animations setNeedsRender if one animation has actually run.
needsRedraw will be set whenever the window or framebuffer
renderFrame: is always running tied to the frameRate.
A display is a render step and a refresh step.
The rendering is done in three steps.
* The view hierarchy is drawn into a framebuffer.
The refresh is done in two steps.
* The offscreen framebuffer is used to refresh the screen
